name: Qin dynasty

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 2,433,000 km2 for 210 BCE (mid); Taagepera 1979 gives 2.3 million for 220 BCE (Qin dynasty page, low). The union of the world_bc300 Qin and Zhou states polygons (the states Qin had conquered by 221) measures 2.47 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_bc300.geojson).

population.note: Seshat codes 40 million for 207 BCE (mid). The first census (2 CE, Han) counted 57.7M (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty) after two centuries of growth; the unification wars killed and displaced many, so the low end is well below. No Qin census survives.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Xianyang ~200,000-350,000 (Seshat 250); Linzi, Handan and Ying were large cities; >90% rural (Lewis 2010 p. 102).

activePersonnel.note: Field army of 600,000 (Wang Jian against Chu 224-223, and Wang Ben's 600,000 in 225, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin%27s_wars_of_unification) + ~100,000 garrisons in the conquered states = 700,000. Shiji figures repeated by modern narratives; in 214 BCE ~100,000 held the north and 500,000 went south (Morton 1995 p. 47, on the Qin dynasty page); Meng Tian led 300,000 against the Xiongnu (215). Chronicle-derived; modern scholars (Lewis) accept armies of hundreds of thousands under universal service. Mid 700,000 for the armies still mobilised at unification; grade C.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Every registered adult male had served; men of recently demobilised conquest armies could be recalled within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Supply trains, engineers, canal and river boat crews (e.g. the Lingqu canal built for the southern campaign), staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Qin registered all adult males for service (registration of ages from 231 BCE, Sanft via the Qin dynasty page); Changping 260 BCE reportedly drew every male over 15 in Henei. Total war fraction of the whole population a few to ten percent.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess: heavy infantry with ji halberds, spears and lamellar, the bulk of the active total; Terracotta Army pits show armoured infantry as the main arm.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: standardised bronze and iron weapons from state workshops

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: universal service with twenty-rank merit system (Hui 2005, Qin dynasty page)

count.note: Educated guess. Crossbowmen and archers; Needham credits the Qin with up to 50,000 crossbows in service (Military of the Han dynasty page), a floor for crossbows alone.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: trigger crossbow with standardised parts, the best missile weapon of its age

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: drilled conscripts

count.note: Educated guess. Light troops, convicts and labour levies used as skirmishers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: light equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: levies and convicts

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted archers, a minor arm before Han expansion (cavalry figurines in pit 2).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: no stirrups, light horse

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: frontier recruits

count.note: Educated guess. Chariots still in service as command and shock vehicles (Terracotta pits hold over 100 chariots).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: obsolescent arm

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: aristocratic drivers

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (proven commanders). Evidence: Wang Jian, Wang Ben, Meng Tian conquered six states in ten years (230-221)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: rank-for-heads merit system and collective punishment units of five

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (recent victories). Evidence: unbroken run of victories ending in unification

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (300 BCE iron weapons). Evidence: trigger crossbows, bronze and iron blades, ji halberds

armor.note: Anchor: between 2 and 3. Evidence: lamellar of leather and some iron; stone lamellar suits in the mausoleum

ships.note: Anchor: 2 (oared war galleys). Evidence: river craft; the 219 BCE sea expeditions came later

fortification.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: rammed-earth city and frontier walls, linked into the long wall after 215

logistics.note: Anchor: 3 (engineered roads, depots). Evidence: Zhengguo canal (246 BCE), granaries, standardised axle widths

communications.note: Anchor: 3 (mounted relay posts). Evidence: postal relay and beacon signalling

isr.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: household registers and spies; little long-range scouting

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no China value before 1000 (1,225); its year-1 values for other agrarian empires are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, France 956 (2011 int$). Early imperial China placed in that band, below the Song level.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A state organised for war; mid is a wartime share at the end of the unification wars.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. State iron and bronze workshops, mass-produced weapons; agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Irrigated Guanzhong and Sichuan (Dujiangyan) granaries fed the conquest armies.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Pre-unification state roads; the imperial highways and Straight Road were built after 220-212.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Langya and other Shandong coastal ports; mainly river ports.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Negligible sea-going merchant fleet.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Grain carts and river transport; the Lingqu canal shows the limits in the south.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen and horses of an agrarian population of ~30M.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: Guanzhong ringed by passes (Hangu, Wu) and fortified cities; newly conquered east gives less.

notes: Snapshot at unification, 221 BCE, when the conquest armies were still mobilised. Army sizes come from the Shiji as repeated in modern narratives (Morton, Bodde); they are chronicle claims and the grade stays C. The 1,200,000 vs 1,500,000 strengths in the Wikipedia infobox are uncited and not used. Border: the union of world_bc300 Qin and Zhou states, i.e. the lands Qin had conquered; it omits the later southern (Baiyue) conquests of 214. Population convention: everything inside that border. GDP per capita is a regional analogy (grade D). Personnel: active = conscripts actually under arms in the conquest armies and garrisons at unification; trainedReserves = registered men who had served and were demobilised; mobilizable = population x ratio.
